statement: Which of these numbers cannot be written as the sum of two or more consecutive positive whole numbers?

choices.misconception: I thought a perfect square such as 45 squared could not be split into a run of consecutive whole numbers.
I thought an even number could never be such a sum, because two consecutive numbers always add up to an odd number, and I did not try longer runs.
I thought a prime number could not be split into consecutive numbers, since it has no factors to work with.
I knew that powers of 2 behave specially and assumed every power, including 3 to the power 7, behaves the same way.

hints: Write a run of k consecutive numbers starting at a, and add it up.
The run a, a + 1, ..., a + k - 1 adds up to k(2a + k - 1)/2. Its two factors differ by an odd number, so one is odd. Which choice has no odd factor above 1?
Suppose 2048 were such a sum. Then k(2a + k - 1) = 4096, and both factors are at least 2.

solutions.reliable: Suppose 2048 = a + (a + 1) + ... + (a + k - 1) with k at least 2 and a at least 1. Adding up, k(2a + k - 1) = 4096. The factors k and 2a + k - 1 differ by 2a - 1, which is odd, so one of them is odd; and both are at least 2. But 4096 is 2 to the power 12 and has no odd factor bigger than 1, a contradiction. So 2048 cannot be written this way. The other four can: 2025 = 1012 + 1013, 2027 = 1013 + 1014, 2187 = 1093 + 1094 and 2026 = 505 + 506 + 507 + 508. The transferable idea: assume the thing can be done, write it as algebra, and follow it until something impossible appears.
solutions.elegant: Every odd number 2m + 1 is m + (m + 1), which knocks out 2025, 2027 and 2187 at once. Between 2026 and 2048, the power of 2 is the one with no odd factor to build a run from.

whyOnTest: Showing the other four sums takes a line each, but ruling out 2048 needs a proof by contradiction: assume a run exists and it forces an odd factor that 4096 does not have.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
